rv.q: Welcome aboard the Barracuda, a floating casino and discotheque of dubious construction. It's 1979 and we're anchored to a pier in New York City's Hudson River, but about to set sail on a side-splittingly funny evening of singing, dancing and near-death experiences.

Even appreciating the gratification of nostalgia and camp, Disaster! is an odd property to find on Broadway and doesn’t seem particularly at home here, with its cheap sets, shabby projections and understaffed chorus.
And so many chances for sharp contemporary satire go begging.
Very little of the dumb dialogue here can hold a candle.
Disaster! is a jukebox musical that uses '70s hits to soundtrack a spoof of '70s disaster movies, and it's about as clever as that sounds.
This creation of Sirius radio host Seth Rudetsky is the Broadway season's happiest surprise.
Disaster! is pure maximalism — a big, old-fashioned musical with big numbers and big performances.

The chance to see the likes of Adam Pascal, Kerry Butler, Faith Prince, Roger Bart, and Rachel York tear it up to the disco hits of the 1970s — on a vessel that literally explodes around them — is a thoroughly delightful experience from start to finish.
The show is fundamentally silly, but it's performed with such commitment and crafted with such attention to detail that it becomes genuinely endearing.
It's not sharp enough to be a toothy parody.
By the time “Disaster” was over, I had laughed some, but mostly I was rooting for the piranhas.
For everyone else, though, this "disaster" of a musical might well leave you with a sinking feeling.
Better words would be “lukewarm mess.”
Disaster! is exactly the kind of show that gives jukebox musicals a bad name
The result is so painfully witless it’s hard to tell where the sea-spray ends and the flop sweat begins.

But Seth Rudetsky and Jack Plotnick’s parody (with Drew Geraci) of ’70s disaster movies (Adventure, Towering Inferno) — set to carefully selected Top 40 pop and disco hits– turns out to be too much fun not to love.
But there are enough belly laughs to keep this show afloat
Bottom line – I had a good time.
